question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? When scientists hunt for newly formed impact craters on Mars, seismic monitoring and orbital imaging function as data sources whose roles are ______: once vibrations picked up through seismic monitoring reveal roughly where an impact occurred, researchers can study orbital photographs of that comparatively small stretch of the rocky surface to pinpoint the exact location of a new crater.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The two methods work together, each supplying what the other lacks, so their roles are complementary.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?

Reported Annual Travel Distances in Four Studies of Migrating Animal Populations
Species | Continent | Distance (km) | Measurement method
Mule deer | North America | 772 | RTD
Caribou | North America | 3,807 | GPS
Gray wolf | North America | 2,155 | GPS
White-eared kob | Africa | 400 | RTD

Some studies of migrating animals gauge yearly travel by outfitting individuals with GPS tracking collars. Others instead rely on annual round-trip distance (RTD), which equals twice the distance between the two habitats a population moves between each year. One researcher contends that because GPS captures every movement an animal makes, tracking a population with GPS would produce markedly higher recorded distances than tracking it with RTD would. For instance, it is very likely that the distance reported for the ______
option a: caribou would be greater than 2,155 kilometers if the RTD method had been used.
option b: caribou would be less than 3,807 kilometers if the RTD method had been used.
option c: white-eared kob would be less than 400 kilometers if the GPS method had been used.
option d: white-eared kob would be greater than 3,807 kilometers if the GPS method had been used.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The caribou's 3,807 km came from GPS; since GPS yields higher figures, RTD would give a smaller distance.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Researchers searching for evidence of ancient life in Africa have uncovered many fossilized hominins, including some in a rock formation at the Danakil Depression. To find still older specimens, however—such as early multicellular organisms from the Ediacaran period—scientists must look in other places, like the Ediacaran rock formation at Ediacara Hills in Oceania, because ______
option a: Oceania contains sites with hominins but none with early multicellular organisms.
option b: the hominins at Ediacara Hills are preserved better than those at the Danakil Depression.
option c: early multicellular organisms occur at more sites worldwide than hominins do.
option d: that formation dates to an earlier time than the formation containing the hominins.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Older organisms would be found in an older formation, so the Ediacara Hills formation predates the hominin one.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In eastern Mexico, two enormous statues of human heads left behind by the ancient Olmec civilization are known as Monument 61 and Monument 1. Each is carved from stone and is remarkably heavy. ______ each one weighs more than 5 tons!
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'In fact' intensifies the preceding point that the statues are extremely heavy.

question: Based on the texts, how would Rose and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the assertion by Slater and Mann (Text 1) about the different prevalence of female birdsong in temperate and tropical areas? Text 1: For many years, ornithologists took for granted that a singing Cassin's finch—a species native to temperate North America—had to be a male trying to attract a mate or defend territory. Yet, as Peter J.B. Slater and Nigel I. Mann have pointed out, no such assumption holds for tropical birds, among which females sing just as often as males. Slater and Mann call for more study of this contrast between female birdsong in the tropics and in temperate regions. Text 2: According to Evangeline Rose and colleagues, recent findings show that a female Cassin's finch can sing every bit as well as a male, and female song is in fact more widespread among temperate species than is generally assumed. Because these females sing less often than males and in more muted tones, Rose notes, it is "easy for researchers to miss the quiet and hidden females and focus on the loud and colorful males."
option a: They would grant that the geographic difference in prevalence is genuine but contend that earlier researchers overstated how often male tropical birds sing.
option b: They would suggest that the difference in prevalence may stem from differences in when the mating season occurs among temperate and tropical species.
option c: They would argue that the apparent difference in prevalence may partly reflect a difference in how easily female birdsong and male birdsong can be detected.
option d: They would warn that the seeming difference in prevalence may be an artifact of researchers studying birdsong more often among temperate species than among tropical ones.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Rose stresses that quiet, drab temperate females are easily overlooked, implying detectability skews the comparison.

question: According to the text, which factors seemed to be linked to the behavior of butterflies in Grace Herzel and colleagues' study? Biologist Grace Herzel and her colleagues examined how butterfly coloration and weather conditions relate to butterfly behavior—research that would not have been possible without data gathered by students and other amateur science enthusiasts in the community. Drawing on more than three years of records, the team found that white butterflies were seen on green flowers more frequently than any other butterflies were, and that butterflies fed more often on cloudy days than on other days.
option a: Butterfly color but not weather conditions
option b: Neither butterfly color nor weather conditions
option c: Weather conditions but not butterfly color
option d: Both butterfly color and weather conditions
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Color linked to flower choice and weather linked to feeding, so both factors relate to behavior.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The woodcut Cat and I is the work of American artist Gertrude Abercrombie, who created ______ in 1936.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular antecedent, a single woodcut, calls for the singular pronoun 'it.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In their hieroglyphic writing, the ancient Egyptians recorded measurements with units such as the khefa, a unit of ______ and the sa, a unit of area. The khefa, for example, is rendered as a short, horizontal hieroglyph shaped like the back of a fist.
option a: length, the khar; a unit of volume,
option b: length the khar, a unit of volume
option c: length; the khar; a unit of volume;
option d: length; the khar, a unit of volume;
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Semicolons separate list items that already contain internal commas, correctly punctuating the three units.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Set in a mid-twentieth-century rural Alaskan fishing ______ Mia Heavener's 2019 novel Under Nushagak Bluff tells the story of three Yup'ik women who grapple with the rise of commercial fisheries and other changes affecting their community.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma correctly closes the introductory phrase before the main clause.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Susana Wadgymar is a biologist based at Davidson ______ conducts research on plants.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period splits the two independent clauses, avoiding a comma splice or fragment.

question: Which finding from the model tests, if true, would support the researchers' hypothesis? Throughout history, tall structures such as Hwangnyongsa in South Korea or Ruwanwelisaya in Sri Lanka have challenged their builders, because they are more vulnerable to physical forces than shorter structures are. A building's lower floors, for example, must bear the immense weight of everything above them. To test the hypothesis that steel is better suited than concrete for a tall building's lower floors, researchers built a computer model of two otherwise identical buildings—one with concrete lower floors and one with steel lower floors—and simulated the effects of wind and gravity on them over the course of a century.
option a: When the simulation ended, the building with steel lower floors had a slightly wider base than it had had at the start.
option b: When the simulation ended, the building with concrete lower floors stood several inches shorter than the building with steel lower floors.
option c: When sudden forces set off vibrations during the simulation, those vibrations took longer to die out in the building with steel lower floors than in the one with concrete lower floors.
option d: During the simulation, the building with steel lower floors flexed more in high winds than the building with concrete lower floors did.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The concrete-floored building compressing to become shorter shows steel better withstands the load, supporting the hypothesis.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? The cactus genus Mammillaria includes more than 150 species spread across the Americas, but heavy rainfall and dense, sunlight-blocking vegetation can threaten their survival. Researchers have located members of the genus in nearly every Mexican state, and several species, such as M. schumannii, are confined to a single state. The genus's absence from parts of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range has been explained as a lack of suitable habitat, yet much of the terrain there is famously hard to reach, which suggests that ______
option a: the apparent absence of Mammillaria in parts of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range may result from insufficient exploration of the region.
option b: M. schumannii may have gone unnoticed in parts of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range because it resembles another species.
option c: the dense vegetation and heavy yearly rainfall in parts of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range hinder the survival of Mammillaria species.
option d: the current methods of collecting and tracking Mammillaria species throughout Mexico may cause an overestimation of the number of species in this genus.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because the terrain is nearly inaccessible, the genus may simply be undocumented there rather than truly absent.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In Los Angeles, producer Christine Wetherill Stevenson received an honor when Pilgrimage Bridge was named ______ her play.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between the preposition 'after' and its object, 'her play.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Girl with a Cat is an oil painting by the Welsh artist Gwen John, who created ______ in 1922.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The single painting is a singular antecedent, requiring the singular pronoun 'it.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Angry Cat (Chat Furieux) is a lithograph by the French artist Jean Dubuffet, who created ______ in 1953.
subject: Reading and Writing

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Having endured harsh conditions for hundreds of years, lighthouses such as the La Jument lighthouse off the coast of Brittany, France, illustrate the ______ between ocean forces and marine structures: the relentless pounding of breaking waves requires the structures to be periodically reinforced or redesigned, and those changes may in turn reshape local wave patterns.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The mutual influence—waves altering structures and structures altering waves—describes an interplay.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? ______ the mythological and heroic themes that frequently appear in the work of Ary Scheffer and other establishment painters, Honoré Daumier's painting The Third-Class Carriage turns instead to something decidedly ordinary: working-class passengers riding in a third-class railway car.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Instead' signals that Daumier avoids the grand themes, so 'eschewing' (rejecting) fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Adventures of Indiana Jones in Wenceslas Square in Prague on January 16, 1989—an underground computer game produced anonymously in 1989 as an act of political protest against the then-authoritarian regime of Czechoslovakia—was originally passed around ______, but the game is now readily available online for anyone to play.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A secretly made protest game would have been distributed secretly, so 'surreptitiously' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Studying caterpillars in fragmented forests—once-continuous forests broken into isolated patches by roads or other interruptions—Nicole M. Dallar et al. emphasize that although fragmentation inevitably ______ changes to local ecological processes, those changes will likely affect Parallelia bistriaris, a specialist that eats only a limited number of plant species, more than a species such as Morrisonia confusa, which feeds on several.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Fragmentation produces the ecological changes, so 'engenders' (brings about) is the precise choice.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Synthetic leather is usually petroleum based, but materials scientists seeking an environmentally sustainable substitute have used various bacteria that secrete straight chains of glucose, building a thick mesh of cellulose known as a pellicle, which resembles leather except in color. The conventional method for dyeing leather produces large amounts of wastewater and other unwanted byproducts, so adopting that method would undercut the ecological promise of the pellicle approach. To address this, Kenneth T. Walker and colleagues worked to modify Komagataeibacter rhaeticus bacteria so that they produce a pellicle with embedded pigment cells, thereby letting the pellicle "dye" itself from within.
option a: To describe a consideration that led the researchers to employ an alternative approach to coloring a pellicle that allowed them to achieve their main goal as presented in the text
option b: To indicate the characteristic of conventional synthetic leathers that makes those leathers poorly suited to achieve the researchers' main goal as presented in the text
option c: To illustrate how the researchers adapted the pellicle approach to overcome a potential impediment to their main goal as presented in the text
option d: To concede that the researchers' main goal as described in the text will be challenging to achieve due to the standard coloring approach being impractical for use on a pellicle
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence explains why standard dyeing was unsuitable, prompting the researchers' self-dyeing alternative.
